To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

archease and the DEAD-box RNA helicase Ddx1 are required for tRNA splicing in mammalian cells and that archease is a functional partner of RtcB, an RNA ligase essential for tRNA maturation in all domains of life.
archease and a DEAD-box helicases, DDX1, are tRNA ligases.
archease and the DEAD-box RNA helicase Ddx1 facilitate tRNA splicing in human cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of RNA repair and RNA splicing in eukaryotic cells.
the identification of new proteins involved in the splicing of tRNAs and the elucidation of their molecular function.
the identification of new factors that facilitate tRNA splicing and provides new insight into the mechanisms underlying this essential cellular process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
archease and RTCB are the only essential components of the tRNA splicing complex and that DDX1 is a cofactor.
the human tRNA spliceosome is a complex of at least five proteins, RTCB, DDX1, ARCH, CGI-99 and FAM98B.
archease and RTCB form a functional complex that is required for the tRNA splicing process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
archease is a new tRNA splicing factor that facilitates the formation of the guanylate intermediate central in RNA ligation.
the RNA ligase complex has a role in the repair of damaged RNA and in tRNA splicing.
archease and the DDX1 RNA helicase are required for tRNA ligase function and that the human tRNA ligation pathway involves a guanylate intermediate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNA ligase complex is composed of at least five different proteins.
the human tRNA repair complex is a heteromeric complex of at least six subunits.
we identified archease as a novel component of the tRNA ligase, a protein complex that is required for tRNA splicing and thus for protein synthesis.
